archetype.name: Rebuilding (shootout-prone)
archetype.definition: A franchise two losing seasons removed from its 12-13 win peak, with an aggressive offense that scores more than its efficiency earns and a defense that has fallen apart against the run.

report.headline: Points mask a league-worst run defense and a turnover-prone offense.
report.take:
The Saints are who their record says they are, and arguably a bit worse. At 2-4 with a -26 point differential, their margin implies 2.6 wins, so there is no bad-luck story here. Net EPA ranks 28th, behind the record. This is the third straight down year after the 13-, 13- and 12-win seasons of 2018-2020 (five and six wins the last two years), and Kellen Moore's second season has Tyler Shough starting all six games. That continuity at quarterback is the one stable piece.

The offense scores 25.3 points a game, 10th in the league, on EPA that ranks only 20th. The gap is filled by things around the snap rather than the snaps themselves. Special teams rank 10th in EPA per game. Moore has gone for it on every fourth down that qualified, the most aggressive rate in the league, and the offense converts 82.4% in short yardage. Nine takeaways, 7th, have handed the offense short fields; the Giants win came on four of them. Shough is the swing piece. He threw for 410 yards in Detroit but turned it over three times and took five sacks, then managed 96 yards and -11.9 passing EPA against Minnesota. The ground game gets little help: 3.39 yards a carry and 2.0 yards before contact, 27th.

The defense is the real problem, and it is new. Last year this unit ranked 10th in EPA allowed. Now it is 27th, last in both rush EPA allowed and success rate allowed, giving up 139.3 rushing yards a game. Atlanta ran for 205. The passing yardage allowed looks tolerable until you see the rest: the pass rush ranks 29th in pressure rate, deep-pass EPA allowed is 31st, and the Giants threw for 395 even in a game the Saints won with five sacks. Opponents can either run at them or wait for a deep shot, and the missed-tackle rate (23rd) makes both worse.

Expect the scoring to cool toward what the efficiency supports, while the points allowed stay high unless the run defense is fixed. The next five non-division opponents and Carolina are all .500 or better, so the middle of the schedule is unforgiving. The back end, with Tampa twice, Arizona and Atlanta, is where the wins should come. This looks like another five-to-seven-win season.

strengths.title: Aggression turns drives into points
strengths.body: Moore has gone for it on every fourth down that qualified, the most aggressive rate in the league, and the offense converts 82.4% in short yardage, 6th. That is a big reason the Saints score at a top-10 rate while their offensive EPA sits 20th. The approach is sustainable as long as the short-yardage success holds, though the scoring rate itself should drift down.

strengths.title: Special teams add hidden yardage
strengths.body: The Saints rank 10th in special teams EPA per game, a steady source of field position for an offense that is average snap to snap. Kicking and return value is noisier than offense or defense, but it has been a consistent positive so far.

strengths.title: Pass protection is not the leak
strengths.body: The line ranks 12th in sack rate and 15th in pressure rate allowed, and only 10th-best stuff rate on runs shows it wins at the point of attack more often than the 3.39 yards a carry suggests. Shough's sacks come in bunches (five in Detroit) rather than every week. The issue is creating space for the backs, not keeping the quarterback upright.

concerns.title: Worst run defense in the league
concerns.body: The Saints are last in rush EPA allowed and last in success rate allowed, giving up 139.3 rushing yards a game; Atlanta ran for 205 and Detroit for 165. Poor tackling (23rd in missed-tackle rate) compounds it. With Kaden Elliss, an every-snap linebacker, now out, this is likely to get worse before it improves.

concerns.title: No rush, and deep balls get hit
concerns.body: A pressure rate that ranks 29th leaves the secondary covering too long, and deep-pass EPA allowed ranks 31st. The Giants threw for 395 yards even in a win. That is a structural problem, not variance, and both starting corners are now questionable.

concerns.title: Giveaways sink the offense
concerns.body: The offense has 12 turnovers, including four against Las Vegas and three each against Detroit and Minnesota, all losses. Shough's floor is the issue: the Minnesota game produced -11.9 passing EPA. Some of this is volume and variance, but the Saints cannot cover it with a defense this leaky.

trend.note: Results have swung on turnovers more than on any steady trend: upset wins at Baltimore and New York around a lopsided home loss to Atlanta and a 96-yard passing day against Minnesota. There is no clear upward or downward line yet.

nextGame.headline: Steelers' ground game meets a Saints front missing key pieces
nextGame.body:
This is a Saints home game played in Paris, indoors, with Pittsburgh favored by 3.5 and a 44.5 total. The Steelers are 4-2 but closer to average than the record suggests. Their net EPA ranks 17th, they are 0.83 wins over expected, and they have won three of four one-score games. Their identity is a defense that ranks 6th in EPA and 5th against the pass, paired with an offense that runs well (5th in rush EPA, 4.75 yards a carry) but passes poorly (26th). Yet they still pass well above expectation, 3rd in the league. The Steelers' defense also has soft spots: the league's lowest pressure rate, 29th in missed tackles and 27th in explosive passes allowed.

Availability tilts against New Orleans up front. Linebacker Kaden Elliss (every snap), DT Nathan Shepherd and LB Anfernee Jennings are all out. Both starting corners, Kool-Aid McKinstry (migraine) and Quincy Riley (neck), are questionable, as is guard Cesar Ruiz, who made the trip. WR Jordyn Tyson remains on IR despite traveling. Pittsburgh's receiver room is thinned, with Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson on IR and Ben Skowronek out, and safety DeShon Elliott is on IR.

waysToWin.title: Make Rodgers beat them through the air
waysToWin.body: Pittsburgh's pass offense ranks 26th in EPA and is down two regular receivers, Pittman and Wilson. Its line allows sacks at the 24th-ranked rate. If the Saints can hold up early against the run, the Steelers' habit of passing more than expected plays into the Saints' hands.

waysToWin.title: Clean pockets and shot plays
waysToWin.body: The Steelers generate the least pressure in the league and rank 27th in explosive pass rate allowed. That gives Shough time to push the ball to Chris Olave. Tight ends have also found room against them (24th in EPA allowed to TE1), a fit for Juwan Johnson's 34 targets.

waysToWin.title: Win the hidden yardage
waysToWin.body: The Saints' special teams rank 10th in EPA per game, Pittsburgh's 21st. New Orleans' fourth-down aggressiveness can steal possessions in a game the Book sees as close.

waysToLose.title: Pittsburgh runs through a gutted front
waysToLose.body: Pittsburgh's 5th-ranked run game meets the league's last-ranked run defense, now without Elliss and Shepherd. If the Steelers commit to the ground game, they can move the chains without asking much of a thin receiver group.

waysToLose.title: Another Minnesota-style passing stall
waysToLose.body: Pittsburgh's pass defense ranks 5th in EPA and 5th on short passes, and gets off the field on third down (6th). Against Minnesota's top-ranked defense, Shough produced 96 yards and three turnovers. A repeat here loses the game.

waysToLose.title: Losing the clock
waysToLose.body: The Steelers hold the ball 31.56 minutes a game, 7th, and the Saints allow conversions on 44.6% of third downs, 27th. Long drives would shorten the game and keep the Saints' offense off the field.

nextGame.watch: Pittsburgh's early-down run success against a Saints front missing Elliss and Shepherd: if the Steelers live ahead of the sticks, the Saints' offense never gets enough possessions.

restOfSeason.body: The scoring is the piece most likely to regress. Top-10 points on 20th-ranked EPA leans on fourth-down conversions, special teams and takeaway-driven short fields, and those are harder to repeat than efficient snaps. The defense has more room to improve simply because last-in-the-league run numbers are hard to sustain, and last year's unit was top-10. But the current injuries at linebacker and defensive tackle make a quick fix unlikely. With the Steelers next and then a run of winning-record opponents, the wins should come late, against Tampa Bay, Arizona and Atlanta.
swingFactors: Health of Elliss and the two starting corners
Whether the run defense climbs off the bottom

confidence.note: Six games with a stable QB, but defensive injuries are piling up.
